svg.title: Plain UDP vs Handshaked UDP behind CGNAT
svg.desc: Plain UDP loses the client once the NAT mapping expires or the client's port changes. Handshaked UDP opens the mapping with CONN_REQ, keeps it alive with a constant stream, and follows the client to a new port by its Session ID.

text.tspan: no handshake · no keep-alive · server pins the first client address

svg.text: ✓ client speaks first → NAT opens :40112 → server pins that address
✗ client goes quiet → the mapping expires → server packets are dropped
✗ client comes back on :51873 → server still sends to :40112

text.tspan: CONN_REQ / CONN_ACK · 250 Hz stream · server follows the Session ID

svg.text: ✓ CONN_REQ opens :40112 → CONN_ACK confirms the session
✓ the constant stream doubles as keep-alive → the mapping never expires
✓ NAT moves the client to :51873 → same Session ID → server follows (only in-flight replies are lost)
Slowed down for clarity: the real stream is one packet every 4 ms (250 Hz), and real NAT idle timeouts are much longer.
